dining.name: Mírate
dining.notes: Multi-level rooftop, Tulum-jungle candlelight; bar voted Best in California. Strong chic/date-night + birthday pick. Eastside.

dining.name: Wilde's
dining.notes: Tiny candlelit British bistro/wine bar; bakery-cafe by day. Intimate date-night; tables hard — Notify/bar seats. Eastside.

dining.name: Cafe Stella
dining.notes: Reopened after 2024 closure; slimmed menu — steak au poivre, frisée, frozen-lemon sorbet. Sunset Junction, home turf.

dining.name: Rasarumah
dining.notes: Eastside hotspot (Variety also flagged it). Confirm exact address/neighborhood next pass.

dining.name: Dunsmoor
dining.notes: Restored 1920s building around a huge wood-burning hearth. Eastside, on-profile for a special night.

dining.name: Yess
dining.notes: Grew out of the Yess Aquatic seafood truck. Chef Junya Yamasaki — confirm details next pass.

dining.name: Sushi Nakazawa
dining.notes: Omakase from a Jiro Ono protégé; NYC import's LA debut. Neighborhood unconfirmed.

dining.name: Hermon's
dining.notes: Refreshed chophouse from the Found Oyster team — martinis, pull-apart garlic bread, pasta vongole. Confirm neighborhood.

dining.name: Mish
dining.notes: New-wave deli on La Brea — wood-fired bagels, shakshuka with challah, pastrami reuben on schmaltz-griddled rye.

dining.name: Asadero
dining.notes: Above-average taco stand — smoky asada from a chef who left corporate kitchens. Confirm neighborhood.

dining.name: Amiguita
dining.notes: On the Resy Hit List; details unconfirmed — fill in cuisine/neighborhood next pass.

dining.name: Pasjoli
dining.notes: Refined French bistro, Chef Dave Beran (ex-Alinea). Westside — special-occasion, not walkable.

dining.name: Kassi
dining.notes: Greek-Med rooftop in Venice — mezze, lamb chops, grilled whole fish. Westside.

dining.name: San Laurel
dining.notes: Spanish-inflected dining high in the InterContinental DTLA (José Andrés group).

dining.name: Calabra
dining.notes: Mediterranean rooftop atop the Santa Monica Proper — charred flatbreads, mezze, grilled fish.

dining.name: Found Oyster
dining.notes: Tiny, buzzy seafood bar — clam cakes, chicken-fried oysters. Walk-in/bar; parent of Hermon's. Home turf.

dining.name: Bar Restaurant
dining.notes: Pink-hued, 'strange and fantastic' modern French. Intimate date-night; books up. Sunset Junction, walkable.

dining.name: Sogo Roll Bar
dining.notes: Handroll bar from the Sushi Note team — creative, high-quality fish. Counter seats. Eastside.

dining.name: Lolo Wine Bar
dining.notes: Low-key neighborhood wine bar with a great patio + shareable pasta. Walkable from home.

dining.name: Marco Polo
dining.notes: Outdoor-focused Italian — linguini vongole, gin-arugula cocktails. Patio date-night. Home turf.

dining.name: Clark Street Bakery
dining.notes: Echo Park bakery — caramelized kouign-amann, Nordic breakfast platters. Daytime/casual.

dining.name: Kismet Rotisserie
dining.notes: Casual rotisserie next to Kismet — roast chicken on pita, veg sides. Easy weeknight. Eastside.

dining.name: Jeff's Table
dining.notes: Cult deli hidden behind a liquor store — pastrami, specialty turkey. Lunch. Eastside.

dining.name: Yang's Kitchen
dining.notes: Order-at-counter Taiwanese-Chinese — braised pork rice, beef scallion wraps. SGV-adjacent.

dining.name: Sonmari
dining.notes: Silver Lake handroll spot — inventive DIY rolls (gochujang eel, 'banh mi' albacore). Walkable.

dining.name: Bar Di Bello
dining.notes: Low-lit Milanese-style aperitivo bar — cutlets, branzino, antipasti. Date-night. Home turf.

dining.name: Holbox
dining.notes: Game-changing Mexican seafood stall in Mercado La Paloma — aguachiles, tostadas. Michelin Bib-tier value (confirm). Walk-up.

dining.name: Quarter Sheets
dining.notes: Thick pan-style pizza + great wine list. Bib Gourmand value. Echo Park — walkable from home.

dining.name: Pizzeria Bianco
dining.notes: Chris Bianco's LA outpost (Row DTLA) — among the country's best pizza. Bib Gourmand. Confirm exact address.

dining.name: Sushi Note
dining.notes: Sushi-and-wine bar (team behind Sogo Roll Bar). Valley — a destination, not walkable.

dining.name: Santo
dining.notes: Japanese-Mexican nigiri/handrolls + sake & wine, Sunset Junction. Home turf; next to Bar Seco. (Santō)

dining.name: Bar Seco
dining.notes: Natural wine bar + small plates (CDMX/Madrid/Japan), spills onto Sunset. Walk-in/sidewalk seats. Next to Santo. (aka Seco)

dining.name: Superba
dining.notes: ARI'S ABSOLUTE FAVORITE — food + ambiance, the patio especially (also great inside). Superba Food + Bread, Lincoln Blvd. Westside — worth the drive.

dining.name: L&E Oyster Bar
dining.notes: Silver Lake oyster bar; the upstairs bar is the chill walk-in move. Home turf.

dining.name: Pijja Palace
dining.notes: Indian-Italian sports bar — pizza, pasta, cricket on the TVs. Very popular (hard rez / walk-in bar). Silver Lake, home turf.

dining.name: Night + Market Song
dining.notes: Kris Yenbamroong's fiery northern Thai on Sunset. Walk-in friendly. Home turf.

dining.name: Momed
dining.notes: Mediterranean — mezze, wraps, bowls. Atwater Village (also Beverly Hills). Eastside, easy.

dining.name: Bar Siesta
dining.notes: New Spanish tapas + all-Spanish wine bar (Heather Sperling team). On-taste wine bar, home turf.

dining.name: Atrium
dining.notes: Playful, vaguely-French cooking from Douglas Rankin in the old Malo space, Sunset Junction. New. Home turf.

dining.name: Bowery Bungalow
dining.notes: Modern Mediterranean from George Abou-Daoud in the former Sompun Thai. New, home turf.

dining.name: Frank n Franks
dining.notes: Sandwich spot from a Howlin' Ray's vet. Casual lunch, Chinatown — eastside-adjacent.

events.title: Information - All Vinyl Night w/ Taylor Shockley + Luke Mele + CHOíCE

artist_notes.name: Luke Mele
artist_notes.note: LA-based selector with a long-running NTS Radio show spanning Balearic house, dub techno, ambient and trip-hop — a genuine home-listening digger, exactly the vinyl-only lane you like.

artist_notes.name: Taylor Shockley
artist_notes.note: House/ambient/minimal/dub DJ with credits on Insomniac and Mixcloud — smaller name, limited verifiable bio beyond active gigging.

enrichment.curator_note: A location-TBA all-vinyl night built around Luke Mele's NTS-honed Balearic/ambient/dub sensibility is squarely the listening-bar format worth chasing an address for — quieter and more textural than a peak-time club night.

events.title: Markus Schulz (Open To Close)
events.detail: EDM night at Avalon Hollywood.

artist_notes.name: Markus Schulz
artist_notes.note: German-American trance veteran (Coldharbour Recordings founder, longtime top-10 DJ Mag placement) — progressive trance with techno and D&B influences. Well outside the house/techno lane; a big trance name, not a groove/European-house one.

enrichment.curator_note: A trance open-to-close set is a genuinely different genre from the rooftop-groove and tech-house lane — Schulz is a legitimate name in that world, just not this one, so this is more 'know it exists' than 'go.'
enrichment.description: Markus Schulz plays an open-to-close trance set at Avalon Hollywood, 10pm.

events.title: Thermal w/ Beau Didier, Kyrxmi, Hommes, OTAK, Pierre, Di0rsita

artist_notes.name: Beau Didier
artist_notes.note: Amsterdam DJ/producer (b. 1999) and Vulged co-founder — bass-heavy, vocal-driven hard groove/techno; releases on Molekül and Mutual Rytm, plays HÖR Berlin and Awakenings.

artist_notes.name: Kyrxmi
artist_notes.note: Phoenix-via-LA techno DJ, EvilGroove label affiliate — deep, driving, hypnotic groove techno for the SoCal TBA-warehouse circuit.

artist_notes.name: ÖTAK
artist_notes.note: Recurring Thermal support DJ — hard/industrial techno, releases on 44 Label Group and Dolma Records; a known quantity on this specific circuit rather than a marquee name.

enrichment.curator_note: Closer's Thermal nights are the real hard-techno TBA-warehouse afterhours in this city — Beau Didier's bass-heavy groove alongside ÖTAK's industrial edge makes this one for people who actually want to be up at 4am, not a casual stop.
enrichment.description: Closer's Thermal series returns for an 11pm-5am TBA DTLA warehouse afterhours with Amsterdam hard-groove techno DJ Beau Didier, Kyrxmi, and ÖTAK.

events.title: House Of Efunk: INVT, Papa Lu, Soul Clap, Special Guest, Stacy Christine x DJ Kerry

artist_notes.name: INVT
artist_notes.note: Miami duo (Luca Medici & Delbert Perez) — sound-system club music fusing dub, UK bass, and Latin-rooted percussion; play DC-10/Circoloco, Fabric, and Panorama Bar.

artist_notes.name: Papa Lu
artist_notes.note: Bay Area-to-LA DJ/producer spanning disco to techno, Kazbah (Burning Man) co-founder — plays everything from underground rooms to EDC/Escape-tier festivals.

artist_notes.name: Soul Clap
artist_notes.note: Boston/NY house duo (Eli Goldstein & Charles Levine) — House of EFUNK is literally their own decade-plus-running party brand, built on funky, eclectic house/disco/boogie; longtime Wolf + Lamb/Crew Love crowd.

artist_notes.name: Stacy Christine
artist_notes.note: LA warehouse-scene DJ since 2012 (Music For Dancers, Critter Control, Machine Club lineage) — joyful house into kinetic techno; has opened for DJ Harvey, Moodymann, and Honey Dijon.

artist_notes.name: DJ Kerry
artist_notes.note: LA DJ since 2005, longtime Dublab radio host and founder of The Basement, a membership-based party rooted in Paradise Garage/West Coast warehouse tradition.

enrichment.curator_note: Soul Clap headlining their own decade-plus party brand, with Stacy Christine and DJ Kerry — two of the names actually holding down LA's warehouse-disco scene — also on the bill, makes this a stacked funk-forward day-into-night pick.
enrichment.description: Day-into-night house party (5pm-3am) at The Bridge from Midnight Lovers' House of EFUNK series, headlined by Soul Clap with INVT, Papa Lu, Stacy Christine, and DJ Kerry.

events.title: Disconic presents Junior, Kana Hishiya, John Smith with bilal

artist_notes.note: Japan-born, LA-based DJ/producer — house and techno moving between punchy, minimal and broken-beat, with dreamy melodic turns; played MEOKO and Sirens LA podcast series.

artist_notes.name: bilaliwood
artist_notes.note: NYC/LA DJ, ex-child actor — plays tasteful, left-of-center selections across genres; regular on the DāM-Funk/Fusicology TBA-party orbit.

enrichment.curator_note: A Disconic TBA lineup with real depth on paper — Kana Hishiya's melodic house/techno range and bilaliwood's crate-digger reputation both check out — but Juniör and John Smith don't have a verifiable footprint, so treat this as a solid-not-certain underground bet.
enrichment.description: Disconic presents Juniör, Kana Hishiya, John Smith and bilaliwood at a TBA Los Angeles location, 11pm.

artist_notes.name: DJ Noir
artist_notes.note: LA selector (Phyliss Jaxson) affiliated with Juke Bounce Werk and dublab's radio community — footwork/juke and bass-leaning sets.

artist_notes.name: Boo Lean
artist_notes.note: Lauren Goshinski — NYC/LA selector, VIA Festival co-founder, now a Public Records/Lot Radio resident; eclectic, genre-blurring sets moving through dub, drum-play and melodic vocal house.

artist_notes.name: Spiñorita
artist_notes.note: Angela Ramirez — Alhambra-raised Chicana DJ and host of NTS's Casual Play; disco, house, funk and vinyl-digging roots, a fixture of LA's underground/backyard party scene since 2010.

enrichment.curator_note: Four deep, genre-blurring LA selectors on a dublab-curated bill at a scrappy Lincoln Heights bar — this is the vinyl-digging, eclectic-groove night the lane exists for, and it's close to home.

enrichment.curator_note: This is full-tilt 200 BPM gabber/hardcore, not house or techno — a clear miss for this lane unless that's specifically what you're chasing tonight.

artist_notes.name: Stephan Bodzin
artist_notes.note: German melodic-techno mainstay known for full live hardware/modular sets — cinematic, emotive techno in the Afterlife/Tale of Us vein, running his own Herzblut label since 2006.

artist_notes.name: DENYC
artist_notes.note: LA-based artist (Denise Poole) blending live vocals with dance-heavy basslines — still emerging, limited track record.

enrichment.curator_note: Bodzin's live rig sets are the rare melodic-techno booking that's actually musical rather than just pretty-sounding — a pier is an odd but fun setting for it.

events.title: WORK presents: Ken Ishii, Phara, & yNOTi

artist_notes.name: Ken Ishii
artist_notes.note: Japanese techno pioneer since the mid-90s R&S Records run — 'Extra,' with its Koji Morimoto (Akira)-directed video, is a genre touchstone; now releases on his own 70 Drums imprint. A real legacy booking.

artist_notes.name: Phara
artist_notes.note: Brussels DJ, a Fuse resident since 2016 — vinyl-only sets pulling from Detroit/Berlin/UK techno plus post-punk and EBM, runs the Phaaar label.

artist_notes.name: yNOTi
artist_notes.note: LA techno DJ/producer (Sydney J) with classical-violin training — dark, driving techno; has shared bills with Truncate and SPFDJ, a rising local name.

enrichment.curator_note: Ken Ishii is a genuine 90s techno legend and Phara's a proper Fuse-Brussels vinyl selector — a rare TBA bill with real international pedigree instead of just local warehouse regulars.
enrichment.description: WORK's TBA LA warehouse afterhours with 90s techno pioneer Ken Ishii, Brussels' Phara, and LA's yNOTi, 11pm.

artist_notes.name: Doc Martin
artist_notes.note: West Coast house pioneer — moved SF to LA in the early '90s, founded the long-running Sublevel label/party (25 years deep in 2026); deep, tribal, acid-inflected house from a genuine scene elder.

artist_notes.name: Lee Burridge
artist_notes.note: UK DJ, founder of All Day I Dream — melodic, organic, Balearic-leaning house; about as close to the European sunset-groove reference point as a festival lineup gets.

artist_notes.name: Justin Martin
artist_notes.note: Dirtybird co-founder — bouncy, quirky, bass-inflected West Coast house ('Sasquatch', 'Buggin''); SF scene royalty.

artist_notes.name: Radio Slave
artist_notes.note: Matt Edwards' techier alias — Rekids co-founder, ex-Ministry of Sound resident; propulsive, muscular house/techno, a genuinely European-pedigreed booking.

artist_notes.name: Mikey Lion
artist_notes.note: Desert Hearts co-founder — psychedelic house/techno out of the SoCal camping-rave scene, warmer and trippier than straight club fare.

artist_notes.name: DJ Colette
artist_notes.note: Chicago house vocalist/DJ (Om Records, Skint) — classic Chicago-lineage vocal house, been in the game since the late '90s.

artist_notes.name: Anton Tumas
artist_notes.note: Subtract Music founder — deep house/techno/hypnotic-electronica selector who ran the beloved 'Subtract On The Pier' Long Beach series; genuinely well-regarded in the SoCal deep-house underground.

artist_notes.name: DAVI
artist_notes.note: Armenian-born, LA-based progressive house producer — early support from Hernan Cattaneo, Nick Warren, John Digweed; polished melodic-prog rather than raw underground.

artist_notes.name: DJ Minx
artist_notes.note: Detroit house matriarch, Women on Wax founder — tracked artist; deep, soulful, dancefloor-first selection.

enrichment.curator_note: This is a real house-music bill, not a generic festival dump — Doc Martin and Lee Burridge alone give it actual lineage, and DJ Minx (already tracked) plus Radio Slave add European/Detroit weight. Long Beach is a haul, but the depth of this lineup earns it.
enrichment.description: Love Long Beach Festival at Shoreline Aquatic Park, 2pm, with a house/tech-house lineup including Doc Martin, Justin Martin, Lee Burridge, Radio Slave, Mikey Lion and DJ Minx.

artist_notes.name: DJ Slugo
artist_notes.note: Chicago ghetto-house/footwork pioneer, founding Dance Mania crew alongside DJ Deeon and Paul Johnson — raw, high-BPM, chant-hook club tracks; the sound Daft Punk sampled on 'Teachers.'

enrichment.curator_note: Baile World is one of LA's best global-club rooms (founded by DJ CQUESTT, built around femme/POC selectors), and landing a Dance Mania originator like DJ Slugo is a real coup — footwork/ghetto-house rather than straight house, so know what you're walking into, but it'll move.

artist_notes.name: Demuir
artist_notes.note: Toronto-based, Chicago-schooled house producer — Beatport's #1 Jacking House producer 2015/2016, credited with creating the 'Jackin House' genre tag; 600+ tracks deep, releases on Hot Creations and Classic. Funky, sexy, groove-first house.

enrichment.curator_note: Certified Groovers keeps booking real house heads for these TBA nights, and Demuir's jackin'-house pedigree (he basically named the subgenre) makes this a solid groove-forward pick over a lot of the generic 'electronic, TBA' listings this week.
enrichment.description: Certified Groovers presents Demuir at a TBA downtown LA location, 10pm.

events.title: HARD Summer Music Festival
events.detail: Open-air fest HARD Summer returns with a globe-trotting line-up boasting Tokischa, salute, Charlotte de Witte, Zack Fox, Shygirl, VTSS and hometown heroes CQUESTT and Dj Warning.

artist_notes.name: Charlotte de Witte
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno powerhouse, KNTXT label boss — hard, hypnotic peak-time techno; a tracked name and one of the strongest bookings on this lineup.

artist_notes.name: Boys Noize
artist_notes.note: Berlin electro/techno veteran (Alex Ridha) — distorted, industrial-leaning club music going back to the mid-2000s Boysnoize Records run; still a reliably weird, high-energy set.

artist_notes.name: Maceo Plex
artist_notes.note: Miami-via-Barcelona producer (Eric Estornel) — tech-house and techno crossover, Ellum Audio boss; deep, dark, groove-driven.

artist_notes.name: Tiga
artist_notes.note: Montreal electro-house institution (Turbo Recordings) — tongue-in-cheek, disco-inflected electro; a real name for the older end of this bill.

artist_notes.name: VTSS
artist_notes.note: Polish DJ/producer on the harder, rave-leaning end of techno — Bicep's Fabric label, T4T LUV NRG co-founder; a genuinely respected underground name amid the festival billing.

artist_notes.name: Shygirl
artist_notes.note: UK rapper/vocalist and NUXXE co-founder — hyperpop-adjacent club music, Sega Bodega/Arca collaborator; more art-club than DJ set.

artist_notes.name: Hannah Laing
artist_notes.note: Scottish DJ/producer on the UK hard-house/hardcore-revival wave — high-BPM, rave-nostalgic tech house.

artist_notes.name: Vintage Culture
artist_notes.note: Brazilian tech-house export, Solotoko boss — tracked name; huge festival draw, big-room but genuinely well-selected house.

artist_notes.name: Mau P
artist_notes.note: Dutch producer of 'Drugs From Amsterdam' fame — tracked name; big-room tech house with a raw, jacking edge.

artist_notes.name: DJ Seinfeld
artist_notes.note: Swedish-Argentine producer (Armand Jakobsson) who pioneered 'lo-fi house' — tracked name; hazy, nostalgic house that's a shade more tasteful than most of this bill.

artist_notes.name: Chris Lorenzo
artist_notes.note: UK bass/house producer, Half Baked label — tracked name; UK garage-inflected, bass-heavy house.

artist_notes.name: Interplanetary Criminal
artist_notes.note: Manchester producer riding the UK bassline/2-step revival — one of the more interesting names on the bill if you like that skippy, rave-adjacent garage sound.

artist_notes.name: Amelie Lens
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno star, Exhale label — tracked name; driving, hypnotic peak-time techno with real European club credibility (see also her own Grand Park date this batch).

artist_notes.name: Andy C
artist_notes.note: UK drum & bass legend, RAM Records boss — outside the house/techno lane but a genuine, decades-deep DJ talent if you catch a set.

artist_notes.name: Etari
artist_notes.note: LA-based (Orange County-raised) producer and AUNTIE co-founder — house through trance and techno, with releases on 100% Silk; regular on the Lights Down Low/HARD Summer circuit.

artist_notes.name: Nick León
artist_notes.note: Miami producer on TraTraTrax and Future Times — fuses dembow, reggaeton and dancehall rhythm into house/techno (his own coined term: 'arquitectronica'); one of the more genuinely distinctive club producers right now, sun-bleached and heavy in equal measure.

events.title: HARD Summer Music Festival

artist_notes.name: Knock2
artist_notes.note: US producer straddling bass music and pop-leaning electronic — big festival-stage energy, outside the house/techno lane.

artist_notes.name: Amelie Lens
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno star, Exhale label — tracked name; driving, hypnotic peak-time techno with real European club credibility (see also her own Grand Park date this batch).

artist_notes.name: Andy C
artist_notes.note: UK drum & bass legend, RAM Records boss — outside the house/techno lane but a genuine, decades-deep DJ talent if you catch a set.

artist_notes.name: Tiga
artist_notes.note: Montreal electro-house institution (Turbo Recordings) — tongue-in-cheek, disco-inflected electro; a real name for the older end of this bill.

artist_notes.name: Vintage Culture
artist_notes.note: Brazilian tech-house export, Solotoko boss — tracked name; huge festival draw, big-room but genuinely well-selected house.

artist_notes.name: VTSS
artist_notes.note: Polish DJ/producer on the harder, rave-leaning end of techno — Bicep's Fabric label, T4T LUV NRG co-founder; a genuinely respected underground name amid the festival billing.

artist_notes.name: Boys Noize
artist_notes.note: Berlin electro/techno veteran (Alex Ridha) — distorted, industrial-leaning club music going back to the mid-2000s Boysnoize Records run; still a reliably weird, high-energy set.

enrichment.curator_note: Day two of HARD Summer is the thinner bill for this lane — Amelie Lens and Vintage Culture again, but otherwise skews bass/hyperpop. Only worth it if you're already at the grounds from day one.

artist_notes.name: Nikki Nair
artist_notes.note: Atlanta producer/DJ blending techno, electro, breaks and UK bass into something genre-agnostic and physical — releases on Dirtybird and Lobster Theremin, mentored early by Underground Resistance's Mike Banks.

artist_notes.name: George Daniel
artist_notes.note: The 1975's drummer moonlighting as a dance producer/DJ — founded the label dh2 out of afterparty DJ sets; plays bass-leaning, UK-rap-inflected electronic sets, not a genre veteran but a genuine crate-digger's side project.

enrichment.curator_note: Lights Down Low has been LA/Bay Area's best-kept afterhours secret for over a decade, and Nikki Nair is one of the most inventive bass-techno hybridizers going right now — a real reason to stay out late even with a curiosity booking like George Daniel on the same bill.

artist_notes.name: Tauceti (FR)
artist_notes.note: French techno/ambient producer with a growing profile in that scene — couldn't pin down a label home, so treat this as a promising rather than proven booking.

artist_notes.name: Mha iri
artist_notes.note: Edinburgh-raised, Melbourne-forged techno DJ/producer — big-room-meets-emotional sound with her own vocals, now signed to PIAS and releasing on Adam Beyer's Drumcode; genuinely on the rise (Awakenings, Tomorrowland, Hï Ibiza in the last year).

artist_notes.name: Gerard Not Gerald
artist_notes.note: Co-founder and resident of INCOGNITO itself (formerly Franco Benito) — has held down LA's underground techno scene for over a decade, sharing decks with Kevin Saunderson, Kenny Larkin and DJ Pierre.

enrichment.curator_note: Mha iri's Drumcode pedigree is the real signal here — a proper warehouse booking from a promoter that's been quietly building LA's underground techno scene for a decade.

artist_notes.name: EMBRZ
artist_notes.note: Dublin producer (Jack Casey) making atmospheric, vocal-forward melodic house — signed to Lane 8's This Never Happened label; downtempo-leaning and emotive rather than peak-time.

enrichment.curator_note: A rooftop sunset set from a This Never Happened-orbit artist is squarely the golden-hour-groove lane — EMBRZ leans dreamier and more vocal than a straight house DJ, good for the early slot rather than the whole night.

events.title: Midnight Lovers with Isaac Carter, Harrison BDP, Lubelski

artist_notes.name: Isaac Carter
artist_notes.note: London DJ/producer, vocal-led deep house on his own Ochi imprint — championed by Ben UFO, Joy Orbison and Seth Troxler; UK-club lineage (Chicago/Detroit roots filtered through contemporary UK dance).

artist_notes.name: Lubelski
artist_notes.note: LA producer (Jake Lubell) making analog, vinyl-informed house with a wide festival footprint (Lightning in a Bottle, Desert Hearts, Dirtybird Campout) — eclectic and percussive rather than a strict selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Isaac Carter's UK deep-house pedigree (that Ben UFO/Seth Troxler co-sign carries real weight) makes this a stronger TBA-DTLA afterhours than the billing alone suggests — a legit late-night option once Harrison BDP fills in the middle.
enrichment.description: TBA-location DTLA afterhours (starts midnight) with London deep-house producer Isaac Carter, Welsh DJ Harrison BDP, and LA's Lubelski.

artist_notes.name: Phantoms
artist_notes.note: LA duo (Kyle Kaplan, Vinnie Pergola) blurring house and indie-dance — 'alternative electronic,' now on Foreign Family, ODESZA's label. Bigger-room, hooky and radio-adjacent rather than a selector's set.

enrichment.curator_note: This is DTLA pool-party energy from a duo built for festival middle-slots, not the rooftop-groove thing — fine if you want an afternoon out at Level 8, but there's no real DJ-selection angle here.
enrichment.description: Daytime pool party at Level 8 DTLA headlined by LA electronic duo Phantoms, 2pm start.

artist_notes.name: Action/Adventure
artist_notes.note: Touring pop-punk band rounding out the bill alongside Like Roses on this Driveways run.

enrichment.curator_note: This isn't the rooftop-house lane at all — straight all-ages pop-punk/emo — but as the live-band side of the taste goes, three real touring bands on one bill beats a single support slot as an afterthought.

artist_notes.name: Shonky
artist_notes.note: Paris house/tech-house lifer (Olivier Ducreux) — a third of the Apollonia trio with Dan Ghenacia and Dyed Soundorom; groovy, stripped-back underground house, well-suited to an extended set.

artist_notes.name: Silky
artist_notes.note: London house/techno DJ mentored by Frankie Knuckles — works the grey zone between deep house and techno, with releases on Culprit and My Favorite Robot.

artist_notes.name: Enzo Muro
artist_notes.note: Peruvian-born, LA-based house/techno selector and a resident of Dialogue itself — patient, flow-first sets; also co-runs the vinyl-only YouKnowWhat label/party.

artist_notes.name: Lubelski
artist_notes.note: LA producer (Jake Lubell) making analog, vinyl-informed house with a wide festival footprint (Lightning in a Bottle, Desert Hearts, Dirtybird Campout) — eclectic and percussive rather than a strict selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Shonky's extended set is the real draw — a founding third of the Apollonia crew doing groovy, stripped-back house — and Dialogue's own resident Enzo Muro plus LA's Lubelski keep the afternoon honest.
enrichment.description: Daytime dance party at DTLA's The Bridge headlined by an extended set from Paris tech-house veteran Shonky, with Silky, Enzo Muro and Lubelski.

artist_notes.name: Die Spitz
artist_notes.note: All-female Austin punk band (signed to Jack White's Third Man Records) known for riotous, chaotic live shows — has opened for Foo Fighters, Amyl and the Sniffers, and Sleater-Kinney.

enrichment.curator_note: Olivia Rodrigo's first festival is a genuinely stacked, curated bill — Bikini Kill next to Mitski next to Stevie Nicks is a real lineup, not just a pop show — but it's Irvine on a Saturday and this isn't the electronic lane at all, so it's more 'worth knowing about' than 'worth the drive' unless the day is already built around it.
enrichment.description: Olivia Rodrigo's all-women debut festival at Great Park Live, Irvine, with Chappell Roan, Doechii, Mitski, Garbage, Bikini Kill, The Breeders and guests Stevie Nicks, Karen O and Sarah McLachlan.

artist_notes.name: Massimiliano Pagliara
artist_notes.note: Italian-born, Berlin-based DJ/producer with residencies at Berghain/Basement — Chicago house, Italo-disco and electro-disco worked through analog '70s/'80s hardware; a genuine Live at Robert Johnson / Ostgut Ton pedigree, deeply in the European lane.

artist_notes.name: James Axon
artist_notes.note: LA-based DJ (dublab resident, 'Hearing Color') and founder of the queer underground party Planet Love — deep house, dreamy techno, Italo, Balearic and psych-disco; a real musician's ear (former pianist), has played alongside Octo Octa, Eris Drew, Derrick Carter.

artist_notes.name: Masha Mar
artist_notes.note: Serbian-born, LA-based DJ/curator (the Midnight Lovers crew) with NTS and Dublab residencies — Italo disco, house and dancefloor edits.

enrichment.curator_note: Massimiliano Pagliara headlining Midnight Lovers is a legitimate European-club booking — Berghain-lineage electro-disco with Masha Mar and James Axon rounding it out with LA's own deep-house/dublab crowd. This is the kind of night the fabric-London comparison is actually built for.

events.detail: Amelie Lens takes over Grand Park for a dynamic, extended day-to-dusk set spanning techno, acid, trance and more, Belgium style.

artist_notes.name: Amelie Lens
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno star, Exhale label — tracked name; driving, hypnotic peak-time techno with real European club credibility (see also her own Grand Park date this batch).

enrichment.curator_note: A dedicated day-to-dusk Amelie Lens set at Grand Park, not a shared festival stage — genuinely the better way to catch her than the HARD Summer slot the same month. Extended techno-into-acid-into-trance from a real headliner in a proper Factory 93 room.

enrichment.curator_note: An open-to-close Rich Medina set billed explicitly as house/rare-groove/garage is exactly the deep-crate education worth clearing a whole Saturday night for at a tiki bar like High Tide.

events.detail: The winner of four 2024 Tony Awards®, including Best Musical, is THE OUTSIDERS.Adapted from S.E. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation."In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of ‘outsiders’ battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self- discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. events.title: Bonnie Raitt: Live 2026 with Special Guest Jon Cleary
lineup: Jon Cleary & the Absolute Monster Gentlemen
events.detail: Bluesy singer/songwriter Bonnie Raitt has worked long and hard for her multiple Grammy Awards, hit singles and chart-topping records. Since her 1971 eponymous debut, the California-born performer and long-time activist has steadily maintained a music career, albeit with definite peaks and valleys. The red-headed songstress, one of the only women of her time to play guitar using the bottleneck technique, unleashed seven albums in just nine years, though her big commercial break came with her 10th studio set, 1989’s “Nick of Time.” That 11-track collection, produced by Don Was, earned three Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year. Not only has the Rock and Roll Hall of Famer tackled multiple U.S. tours and international runs, but she’s also a frequent participant in events of social activism, such as Farm Aid and Amnesty International concerts. Raitt’s 16th full-length album and most recent studio release, “Slipstream,” hit retailers in 2012. Not only did ticket sales for the support tour soar, but Raitt also landed the best-selling blues album of the year and took home the Grammy for Best Americana Album.

events.title: THE WHO'S TOMMY
events.detail: In 1969, The Who created a rock opera that changed the course of music history. And now,it’s back in a dazzling all-new production that feels more relevant than ever.Myth and spectacle combine in this fresh reinvention that includes the unforgettable anthems “I’m Free,” “See Me, Feel Me,” “Sensation” and “Pinball Wizard.” After witnessing his father shoot his rival, the young Tommy Walker is lost in the universe, endlessly and obsessively staring into the mirror. An innate knack for pinball catapults him from reticent adolescent to celebrity savior. Tony Award-winning composer Pete Townshend and Tony Award-winning original director Des McAnuff find powerful resonance reexamining this classic story for today.
